question: Is the visitor record I got when I extended my stay the same thing as a Canadian visitor visa?
generated_answer:
No, the visitor record is not the same as a Canadian visitor visa. A visitor record is a document that shows the date by which you must leave Canada. It is issued to people who are already in Canada and need to extend their stay. A Canadian visitor visa, on the other hand, is a document that is required to enter Canada as a visitor. It is issued by a Canadian embassy or consulate outside of Canada.

If you are already in Canada and need to extend your stay, you will need to apply for a visitor record. If you are outside of Canada and need to enter Canada as a visitor, you will need to apply for a Canadian visitor visa.

Here is an example of what a visitor record might look like:

Visitor Record

This document is not a visa. It is a record of your stay in Canada.

Name: [Your Name]
Date of Birth: [Your Date of Birth]
Passport Number: [Your Passport Number]
Date of Entry: [Date of Entry into Canada]
Date of Expiry: [Date by which you must leave Canada]

This visitor record is valid until [Date of Expiry]. You must leave Canada by this date or apply to extend your stay.

If you have any questions about your visitor record or need to extend your stay, please contact Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).
